judgements.justification: A's Reviewer_h7Rc doubted the method suits multi-object tracking because YouTube-VIS is 'mainly for' VOS, which Section 4.1 refutes (classify, segment and track 40 categories); no B reviewer made that error.
B's AC gave a spotlight on ratings 7/6/7/7 with no rating above 7, praising a 'very strong' cost-accuracy trade-off that holds for memory, not speed, on the chair's own reading.
B's raises came from reviewers at confidence 4 with specific points; no high score rested on enthusiasm alone, and A's nMFp gave only a 6 that did not shape A's outcome.
The authors told A only that PCAN is slower than non-local attention (63.2 vs 61.8 ms per frame) and that STMask runs at 28 FPS; B's reply left STMask out and B never saw the runtime comparison.
B's speed and clarity concerns were answered with new results and details, not ignored; the difference in treatment of shared weaknesses is a weighting difference (R08).
After a near-identical rebuttal, B's NPPQ (6 to 7) and HvVc (to 7) raised, while no A score moved.
A's x3ez showed PCAN gains only 0.5-0.6 AP over non-local attention with no runtime gain, and q7JA flagged tuning on the reporting split and missing MAST; no B reviewer raised these.
Both committees saw the same gaps (frame-prototype count, missing details, no KITTI-MOTS, slower than one-stage rivals, modest novelty); B treated them as revision items, A as grounds to reject.
A's AC followed the score count and the reviewers' collective concerns, not a single reviewer.
No reviewer's change is attributed to the other reviews; B's raises cite the rebuttal.
The authors answered x3ez's follow-up with a fixed-memory comparison; x3ez simply did not reply, so no reply was misread or missed.
A's h7Rc (confidence 3, a wrong benchmark claim) and nMFp (four one-line strengths) never engaged after the rebuttal, and both ratings counted unchallenged in A's score count.
A's reject matched three of four ratings below threshold; it did not go against a positive majority.
A's AC decided by the score count but stated no positive assessment of its own; it agreed the reviewers were negative.
A's low scores rested on novelty, efficiency and missing details, which are central, not peripheral.

A's h7Rc and AC read the paper as a pure application paper combining existing techniques without insight, while B's NPPQ and TiXB read it as a new attention mechanism and judged its novelty as a method.
NPPQ admitted not being an MOTS expert and raised, but the rebuttal gave new results (frame-prototype ablation, KITTI-MOTS), not only clarifications.
Where both read the paper the same way, the gap is weighting of shared weaknesses (R08), not an extra requirement for that paper type.
B's NPPQ praised clustering pixels for attention as new ('I couldn't find a work'), though Section 2 cites EM-based prototype attention [19] by the paper's own second author.
A's x3ez wrote 'Most of my concerns are addressed', then called the 0.5-0.6 AP gain 'trivial' and stayed at 5, not answering the authors' fixed-memory reply.
B's HvVc raised to 7 on promised revisions of a paper it called 'badly written', while A's AC listed concerns as if the rebuttal's BDD100K test and KITTI-MOTS results did not exist.
x3ez's 'most concerns addressed' was not a stated change of position to accept, and A acted on the rating, not on that comment.
A's AC cites non-public discussion, but no extra reviewer was called in.
Clarity complaints arose in both committees (HvVc in B, q7JA in A); expertise distance did not split the clarity verdicts.
B's raises came with stated reasons in comments; no silent raise against the review text.
A's AC counted its silent reviewers rather than setting them aside, and B had no silent detractor.
No reviewer in either committee rated above 7.
No reviewer admitted reading only part of the paper.
No reviewer contested the premise from a different theoretical tradition.
B's meta-review argues only for acceptance from 'all four reviewers recommend acceptance' and gives no reason for the spotlight.
A's x3ez and q7JA knew the self-supervised memory-tracker literature and checked the non-local baseline, while B's NPPQ, not an MOTS expert, took novelty at face value and missed cited prior work.

added.name: Area chair misstated reviewers' final positions
added.definition: One committee's meta-review described its reviewers' final positions or the remaining concerns in a way the forum record contradicts, such as calling all reviewers negative when one rated above threshold or omitting results the rebuttal supplied, in the direction of the chair's lower decision.
added.justification: R02 covers a chair overstating consensus to lift a tier; no reason covers a chair misstating the record toward a lower outcome, here calling all reviewers negative against nMFp's unedited 6 and ignoring rebuttal results.

reasoning: Both committees saw the same strengths and largely the same gaps, so the core is weighting (R08) and rebuttal response (R06): B's reviewers raised on a near-identical rebuttal, while A's x3ez said most concerns were addressed yet held 5 (R20) and A's other reviewers stayed silent (R12). Errors pushed both ways: A's h7Rc misread the benchmark (R01), B's NPPQ credited novelty that Section 2 attributes to prior work (R19). A heard things B did not, both from its reviewers (R07, R31) and from the authors (R04). A read the paper as an application, B as a method (R16). B's spotlight has no rating above 7 and no stated case (R02, R30); B credited promises A did not (R21). A's AC misstated the reviewers' final positions, which no reason covered, so I added R32.
